//: Acknowledgements that a counted architecture file changed WITHOUT the census being re-measured. Read by src/scripts/checkCensusFreshness.ts. An entry names the census, the head_commit it was written against (`since`), the FILES it covers, and why those changes cannot have moved a verdict. It covers the paths it names and nothing else — a counted file that changed and is not listed in `files` makes the census stale again, and an entry with no `files` covers nothing. It is spent the moment that census is re-measured: the checker compares `since` against the census head_commit and FAILS on a mismatch, so an acknowledgement cannot outlive the measurement it was written for. A second array, `retired`, holds acknowledgements whose census was later re-declared at a reachable commit: the checker does not read it, and it exists so that the per-file argument that justified the re-declaration survives the entry that carried it.

── ADDED 2026-09-15 by the MIGRATION LANE: 2893's precondition, not its effect ──

WHAT CHANGED. One counted file moved: `artifacts/api-server/src/migrations/2893_rank_events_retire_writerless_surfaces.sql`. The edit is confined to the file's PRECONDITION block — the part that decides whether the migration may run — and touches neither the constraint it installs nor the surfaces it retires.

WHY IT CANNOT MOVE A DISCOVERY VERDICT. Every Discovery row that turns on 2893 turns on WHICH surfaces the file retires and WHETHER any writer still uses them. DV-44 is the row in question, and §41.1 already records the finding that matters: the census's evidence cell names nine writerless surfaces including `living_page` and `watch_feed`, and both halves are false — `routes/mediaFeed.ts` writes `watch_feed` on every media impression and `routes/rankEvents.ts` writes `living_page`, so the nine is seven, and the retirement exists as 2893. None of that is affected here. The retired seven are unchanged (`search`, `nearby`, `story`, `event`, `trip`, `profile`, `explore`); the eight kept are unchanged (`pulse`, `discovery`, `events`, `compass`, `live_pulse`, `living_page`, `watch_feed`, `wall`); the ALTER TABLE that installs them is byte-for-byte what it was; and the SAFETY VETO that counts live rows on a retired surface is untouched and still runs.

WHAT THE EDIT ACTUALLY DOES. The precondition previously recognised ONE starting state — the post-2298 fifteen — and refused everything else with `Apply 2298_dead_check_vocabularies.sql first`. portava-ci already carries exactly the eight this file narrows TO, so the refusal fired on a database where the migration had nothing left to do, and stopped the whole 2891-2970 apply. It now decides three states explicitly: (A) the fifteen, narrow it, unchanged; (B) exactly the eight and nothing else, reconcile and re-assert; (C) anything else, REFUSE and report the live definition rather than assert a diagnosis. Production carries the pre-2298 fourteen and lands in (C), where the refusal is correct and keeps firing. Nothing is skipped in (B) — the DROP/ADD, the safety veto and every postcondition still execute.

WHAT THIS ACKNOWLEDGEMENT IS NOT. It is not a claim that DV-44 is correct; §41.1 says it is not, and that stands. It is not a re-measurement of anything, and it certifies no other row. It says only that a change to WHEN 2893 is allowed to run cannot change a verdict about WHAT 2893 does.

── EXTENDED 2026-09-15: 2910 and 2921, same argument, different mechanism ──

WHAT CHANGED. `2910_discovery_trails.sql` and `2921_creator_earning_entries.sql` were made IDEMPOTENT. Nothing about what they build changed: no column, constraint, trigger body, policy predicate, grant or postcondition was altered. The edits are exactly: `CREATE TABLE` -> `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`; `CREATE [UNIQUE] INDEX` -> `... IF NOT EXISTS`; and a `DROP ... IF EXISTS` placed ahead of each `CREATE POLICY` and each `CREATE TRIGGER` that lacked one.

WHY THEY NEEDED IT. Both files' tables ALREADY EXIST on portava-ci — `content_trails`, `trails`, `trail_edges`, `trail_follows`, `trail_reports`, `trail_health_snapshots`, `creator_earning_entries` — created by a rehearsal that recorded no ledger row, and all of them EMPTY (0 rows, counted). A bare `CREATE TABLE` against them raises 42P07 and stops the applier, which is what would have happened to the 2893-2970 apply immediately after 2893 cleared. This is the same class of defect as 2893's: a migration refusing a database whose state it had already produced.

WHY IDEMPOTENCE IS SAFE HERE RATHER THAN A SILENT PASS. `IF NOT EXISTS` on its own would let a wrong-shaped leftover survive unnoticed. It does not, in these two files, because both re-prove their objects AFTER the DDL and BEHAVIOURALLY: 2910's `$post$` block inserts real probe rows and REQUIRES the label-cap trigger to refuse a second primary Trail and the signal vocabulary to refuse an undeclared signal, then requires the cascade to have removed the probes. A leftover table without those objects fails that block. For the same reason the policies use DROP-then-CREATE rather than `IF NOT EXISTS`: a policy surviving with a DIFFERENT predicate would pass an existence test, so the predicate is re-asserted instead.

WHY NO DISCOVERY VERDICT MOVES. Every Discovery row that turns on these files turns on the objects they install and the behaviour those objects enforce — the Trails label caps, the signal vocabulary, the append-only rule on earnings. All are byte-identical. What changed is only whether the file may run a second time against a database that already carries its effect. Both files remain unapplied on BOTH environments (0 ledger rows on portava-ci and on production), so no recorded checksum is broken by the edit.
